# `kernel/execution/VerifiedTextMutation.js`

> **Source:** `webgpu-os/kernel/execution/VerifiedTextMutation.js`

Content-free, request-bound accounting for verified text mutations. The edit receipt remains the mutation authority because it is built from the complete before/after text after authoritative readback. This module only derives bounded line counts and validates projections of that receipt.

## Functions

### `createVerifiedTextLineStats(before, after, { existedBefore = before != null, existsAfter = after != null, } = {})`

Return exact insert/delete line counts when the bounded Myers search can prove them. Oversized or high-edit-distance inputs return an explicit unavailable state; they are never approximated or counted as zero.

### `createVerifiedTextMutationBinding(value = {})`

### `projectVerifiedTextMutationCandidate(receipt, expected = {})`

Project a content-free candidate before the Faculty verifier settles. This is transport data, not authority; only the kernel may upgrade it with a verified succeeded Faculty receipt whose source hash covers the candidate.

### `normalizeVerifiedTextMutationCandidate(value, expected = {})`

### `projectVerifiedTextMutationSummary(receiptOrCandidate, expected = {})`

Upgrade a candidate only with exact verified succeeded Faculty evidence.

### `normalizeVerifiedTextMutationSummary(value, expected = {})`

Validate an already-projected broker summary before forwarding it.

### `summarizeVerifiedTextMutations(values = [], expected = {})`

Aggregate de-duplicated receipt projections for one exact request/session.

### `normalizeVerifiedTextChangeSummary(value, expected = {})`

### `createUnobservedVerifiedTextChangeSummary(expected = {})`

### `createUnavailableVerifiedTextChangeSummary(expected = {}, integrityFailure = 'line-total-overflow')`

## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```

**See also:** [WebGPU OS Architecture](/webgpu-os/architecture.md) · [Security Model](/concepts/security-model.md)
